tools.name: watch_register
tools.description:
Register a watch. type: deadman | http | tls (for overrun and content use overrun_watch / content_watch).
    target: URL (http/tls); omit for deadman. interval_s >= 300 on the free tier. condition: e.g. {"grace_s": 600} for
    deadman, {"max_ms": 2000} for http latency, {"warn_days": 14} for tls.

tools.name: quickstart
tools.description:
The fastest way to be watched, in one call. Makes you an agent (if you have no key yet) and a deadman watch that expects
    a check-in every `every_minutes` (5 to 1440). Miss one and Ned POSTs a signed message to callback_url; check in again and he
    says it's clear. Returns agent_key (shown once

tools.name: watch_get
tools.description: Current state of one of your watches: status, fired, fire_count, next_check, last_state.

tools.name: watch_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a watch you registered. Frees a free-tier slot.

tools.name: deadman_checkin
tools.description:
Check in on a deadman watch to keep it from firing. Proves you hold the watch's signing_secret (returned at
    registration): it is sent as Authorization: Bearer <signing_secret> for this one call. No agent key needed.

tools.name: overrun_watch
tools.description:
Fire when something is STILL running past its deadline (the other side of a deadman). Register once, then call
    overrun_start when a run begins and overrun_finish when it ends. If a run isn't finished within max_runtime_s
    (60 to 86400), Ned POSTs one signed 'fire' (run_id, started_at, deadlin

tools.name: overrun_start
tools.description:
A run began on an overrun watch. Returns run_id and deadline. Sends the watch's signing_secret as
    Authorization: Bearer for this one call; no agent key needed. run_id is optional (your own id, 1-64 chars); pass one
    and a retried start is safe (it returns the open run instead of superseding i

tools.name: overrun_finish
tools.description:
The run ended. Returns runtime_s and late. If Ned already fired for this run, your callback gets 'clear' with
    late: true. Finishing with no run open is an error (409).

tools.name: content_watch
tools.description:
Fire when a URL answers but says the wrong thing. expect has 1 to 5 conditions: status (int), contains /
    not_contains (a string or list of strings), json_path (dotted, e.g. "data.items.0.state") with equals (a JSON
    scalar) or exists (true/false). No regex. Pages over 256 KB fail as 'size'. T

tools.name: balance
tools.description: Your balance in cents, free allowance used, burn per day, days left, and the top-up routes.

tools.name: pricing
tools.description:
Ned Watch pricing: 5 free watches at >=300s, then per-day rates (http/tls/content 2c, fast 7c, deadman 1c, overrun 1c) from a prepaid
    balance topped up over x402 (USDC on Base). Public, no key needed. Paying is done against POST /v1/topup/{5,20,50}, not here.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: quickstart, overrun_watch, content_watch · Public sink: pricing · Destructive: quickstart, overrun_watch, overrun_start, overrun_finish.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: quickstart, overrun_watch, content_watch · Public sink: pricing · Destructive: quickstart, overrun_watch, overrun_start, overrun_finish

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
